results.content: Consumer confidence fell in September amid worries over the high cost of goods and services, and fuel. Consumer confidence took a dive in September to its lowest reading since 2014 as consumers grew increasingly pessimistic about factors affecting the economy — both for the short and long term. The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index fell by 6.7 points to 81.9 (1985=100) in September, down from 88.6 in August. The Present Situation Index — based on consumers' assessment of current business and labor market conditions — declined by 7.9 points to 109.3. The Expectations Index — based on consumers' short-term outlook for income, business, and labor market conditions — fell by 5.9 points
